summary: Sangseraima Ujeed is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2012–2017). She held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at UC Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Sangye Tenzin (1904–1978) worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, serving as Abbot of Menri Monastery and studying as a doctoral student at the University of Virginia (attested 2026). He taught Matthew T. Kapstein and Lopon Tenzin Namdak.

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and Delhi School of Economics. His posts include the University of Oxford (1993–1995, 2002), EHESS (1995–2002), UCLA (founding director 2005–2011; endowed chair 2014), and Collège de France (2013–2021).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under traditional teacher A. P. Lama and under Mrinal Kanti Gangopadhyay (attested 1994).

Indology and religious studies scholar Sanjukta Gupta earned degrees from Visva-Bharati University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, University of Calcutta, Jadavpur University (~1962–1967), Utrecht University (~1968–1986), and University of Oxford (~1986–2000).

Sanki Ichikawa (1886–1970) was a linguist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1906–1909). He served on the faculty at Tokyo Imperial University (1916–1946) and held a post at the Institute for Research in Language Teaching (~1937–1970).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch works in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Buddhist studies scholar Sao Htun Hmat Win studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at the University of Yangon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).
Sara Frumento is an Indology scholar who studied for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at Wolfson College, University of Oxford (attested 2026).

Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD 2002) under Tom Tillemans and others. She held posts at University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003) and Emory University (attested 2026).

Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (completed by 2016) under doctoral supervisor Jenny Purtle and studied with several scholars, including John C. and Susan L. Huntington.

Sarah E. Fraser works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and she held appointments as Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at EPHE (2000).

Sarah Harding works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (1972) and Lama Tenpa. She was a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2001) and taught at Naropa University (~1992–2018).

Sarah J. Horton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar who studied for an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an M.A. post there (both attested 2026).

Buddhist studies scholar Sarah Shaw studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. Her affiliations include Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies and Wolfson College, and an honorary fellowship at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Saraju Rath is an Indologist who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies (attested 2012 and 2022).

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served as Librarian at the Asiatic Society (1943) and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Presidency Colleges and University of Calcutta. He directed Bhutia Boarding School (1874), served as Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904), and founded the Buddhist Text Society (1892).

Sarat Sarma works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006) under the supervision of S. Shyamkishor Singh, having also studied under S. Lokendrajit Singh.
